items.title: COP31 draft proposes at least $120 billion annually for climate adaptation by 2035
items.summary: The COP31 draft proposes raising annual climate adaptation finance for developing countries to at least US$120 billion by 2035, giving a specific financial target to an earlier commitment to triple funding. It also calls for a roadmap to deliver the money, stronger action to phase out fossil fuels and an end to certain unilateral climate-related trade measures by 2027. The proposals remain subject to negotiations and have not yet been adopted.

items.title: NPP-USA members seek Boadu, Bawumia intervention over election credibility concerns
items.summary: Some members of the New Patriotic Party’s United States branch are calling on John Boadu and Dr Mahamudu Bawumia to intervene over concerns about the credibility of the upcoming NPP-USA elections.

He described the move as a troubling message about how the country chooses to remember its national struggle. items.title: 'Humanitarian mission' for Kostiantynivka: Is it a trap?
items.summary: Russian President Putin has proposed an evacuation of the Ukrainian city of Kostiantynivka, like the recent operation in Oleshky. Experts warn this could serve military, not humanitarian, aims. What should Kyiv do?

items.summary: This week, Iraqi security forces surrounded an area run by the Kataib Hezbollah militia. Onlookers describe it as the most dangerous confrontation between the Iraqi state and Iran-allied militias in decades.

items.summary: The presidents of China, the US and Russia have held an unprecedented summit. While Trump said the three leaders were "making history," Xi described the talks as "fruitful" and Putin called them "open and candid."

items.title: EU Commission confirms it was targeted in cyberattack using AI tools
items.summary: The European Commission was targeted by an "AI-generated cybercampaign," a spokesperson has said. This is the first time the bloc has publicly reported an AI-based cyberattack.

items.title: Wadephul: 'Coalition of the Willing' talks in Berlin send strong signal to Moscow
items.summary: German Foreign Minister Wadephul has said the Coalition of the Willing meeting in Berlin sends a clear message to Moscow to take peace talks seriously. He also warned Ukraine should be prepared for peace talks to fail.

items.title: Pakistan minister to visit India, but no breakthrough expected
items.summary: A Pakistani minister's visit to India for a Shanghai Cooperation Organization forum marks a rare high-level contact between the two archrivals, but analysts say it does not signal a resumption of bilateral engagement.

items.title: Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya, top UN court rules
items.summary: The International Court of Justice has upheld large parts of a genocide case against Myanmar linked to the 2017 conflict with its Rohingya minority. It called for it to pay reparations and let refugees return safely.

items.title: White House fires national cyber director over widespread outages
items.summary: The White House fired national cyber director Sean Cairncross on Thursday following a week of technology disruptions affecting US air travel, email services and national security systems. The departure comes as the Trump administration faces criticism over its response to the outages, which officials say were unrelated incidents.

items.title: PM Sánchez admits 'mistakes' in key debate ahead of Spain's election
items.summary: Spain's Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez acknowledged shortcomings in his government on Thursday as he faced conservative rival Alberto Núñez Feijóo in the campaign's only televised debate. The November 29 election could leave the far-right Vox party in a position to enter government.

items.title: Voyager 1 spacecraft reaches one light-day milestone
items.summary: NASA's Voyager 1 probe, which has been traveling through space for nearly 50 years, hit a milestone distance of one light-day away from Earth on Wednesday. Already the most distant man-made object in the universe, the spacecraft is now about 26 billion kilometers (16 billion miles) away, according to the US space agency. That is the distance a particle of light can travel in 24 hours. FRANCE 24's Emerald Maxwell reports.

items.title: Major anti-gang offensive in Haiti kills 34 suspected gang members
items.summary: Haitian security forces launched a major offensive on Thursday to retake Martissant, a strategic corridor linking Port-au-Prince with the country's western and southern regions that gangs have controlled for five years. Police said at least 34 suspected gang members were killed in clashes involving a private security task force.

items.title: Anthropic goes public after blockbuster IPO but fails to revive AI trade
items.summary: Anthropic has become the first pure-play AI developer to be publicly traded on the stock market, following a record-setting IPO. The stock opened 34% higher, briefly valuing the company at more than $2 trillion, before ending its first day of trading up 17%. However, Wall Street indexes closed sharply lower as investors took profits, reflecting underlying market jitters about the AI trade.

items.title: French far-left candidate Mélenchon opens door to alliance with rival Greens candidate
items.summary: French far-left leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon opened the door to an alliance with France's Greens on Thursday after their presidential candidate Marine Tondelier said she was ready to "work on a coalition around" the veteran leftist. Tondelier's overture has further boosted Mélenchon's campaign for the Élysée Palace – and angered moderates on the centre-left.

items.title: Kenyan marathon champion banned for doping
items.summary: In tonight's edition, Kenyan athletics superstar and reigning marathon world champion Peres Jepchirchir is banned for three years for doping. Also, South African judges leave the courtroom behind and tour a repatriation centre before handing down judgment in 33 emergency asylum applications. And Ghana's presidency has a new jet, but critics of the ruling party are not on board.

items.title: Russian strikes on Kyiv kill one, damage Dutch and Austrian embassies
items.summary: A wave of daytime Russian strikes on Kyiv on Thursday killed one person and damaged a historic cathedral as well as the embassies of Austria and the Netherlands. Loud explosions erupted across the Ukraine capital throughout the day as the leaders of Russia, China and the United States held a historic meeting in China that put Russia's President Vladimir Putin in international spotlight. FRANCE 24's Laurent Berstecher reports.

items.title: Ukraine: Russian strikes damage Austrian and Dutch embassies in Kyiv
items.summary: Russian strikes damaged the Austrian and Dutch embassies in Kyiv on Thursday. Windows were shattered and vehicles damaged, but diplomatic staff escaped unharmed.

items.title: Greenpeace protests at COP31, demands climate finance as island nations face growing threats
items.summary: Greenpeace activists are staging a protest at the COP31 climate talks in Turkey, demanding urgent action. Small island nations are also raising their voices, warning that the climate crisis threatens their very survival. But Greenpeace says progress at the negotiations remains far too slow.

items.title: 48 teams, 104 matches: FIFA U-17 World Cup kicks off in Qatar
items.summary: Qatar is hosting the FIFA U-17 Men’s World Cup, which kicked off on 19 November 2026. It is the second time the country has staged the tournament, following its first hosting in 2025.

items.title: Uganda start U17 World Cup campaign with 3-0 defeat to South Korea
items.summary: Uganda’s Under-17 side, the Uganda Cranes, opened their Group B campaign with a 3-0 defeat to South Korea on Thursday.

items.title: Zimbabwe destroys 250,000 landmines, but funding threatens 2030 clearance goal
items.summary: A major milestone in Zimbabwe's efforts to clear deadly remnants of war. The HALO Trust, the world's largest landmine clearance charity, says it has destroyed 250,000 landmines across the country since 2013.

items.title: Canary island erects field hospital amid migrant influx
items.summary: A sharp rise in migrant arrivals is putting pressure on health services on Spain's Canary Island of El Hierro. Authorities have set up a field hospital at a temporary reception centre to cope with demand. Around 11,000 migrants have arrived since the start of November.

items.title: US: Protesters warn of AI bubble as Anthropic makes stock market history
items.summary: Anthropic made its Nasdaq debut with a record-breaking IPO valuing the AI company at $1.5 trillion. Outside the exchange in New York, police detained three protesters warning of financial risks.

items.title: Gambia pays tribute to Rohingya after ICJ genocide ruling against Myanmar
items.summary: Gambia on Thursday welcomed the landmark judgement of the International Court of Justice that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya minority. Gambia brought the case to the UN’s top court in 2019, two years after Myanmar’s military crackdown against the predominantly Muslim Rohingya.
